history.claim: Originally a monastic residence for forest-dwelling monks, dating back approximately 200 years.
history.quote: merely a monastic residence for forest-dwelling monks

history.claim: Locals call this temple 'Wat Lum' because it is located in a low-lying area.
history.quote: locals usually call it Wat Lum

history.claim: Features an ancient stupa base with a large banyan tree growing on it.
history.quote: stupa base with a large banyan tree growing on it

history.claim: Houses a replica of the Buddha's footprint, Pho Than Kaen Rak, and a jade Buddha image.
history.quote: inside there is a replica of the Buddha's footprint, the sacred Pho Than Kaen Rak

history.claim: Hosts an annual procession of the Buddha's relics on Makha Bucha Day.
history.quote: there will be an annual procession of the Buddha's relics on Makha Bucha Day

history.claim: Secondary tourism sources state that the ordination hall retains early Rattanakosin art.

timeline.title: Temple Appears in Construction/Registration Records
timeline.detail: Local sources indicate 15 May 1893 (2436 BE) and the use of the name Wat Phrathat Khiri Khet.

timeline.title: Granted Royal Boundary
timeline.detail: Local sources indicate the temple was granted a royal boundary (Wisungkhammasima) and is affiliated with the Maha Nikaya sect.

timeline.title: Recorded in the Old Town Plan
timeline.detail: The municipality recorded the old ordination hall, the new one, the replica footprint, Pho Than Kaen Rak, the jade Buddha image, and the relic procession tradition.

timeline.title: Makha Bucha Relic Procession Around the Old Town
timeline.detail: A royal chariot procession carrying the sacred relics takes place around Takua Pa old town, along with a ceremony of circling the vihara three times.

timeline.title: Started as a Monastic Residence for Forest Monks
timeline.detail: Originally a residence for forest-dwelling monks to practice asceticism, dating back approximately 200 years according to official databases.

timeline.title: Replica Buddha Footprint Moved to the Temple
timeline.detail: The replica footprint was once on Khao Phra Bat (Phra Bat Hill), moved to Wat Senanuch Rangsan, and finally enshrined in the ordination hall of Wat Phrathat Khiri Khet.

news.title: Phang Nga Carries 'Sacred Relics' on Royal Chariot Around Takua Pa Old Town
news.summary: The 2025 (2568 BE) Makha Bucha event was held at Wat Phrathat Khiri Khet, featuring a procession around the old town and circling the vihara.

visit.best_time: Morning or late afternoon (according to secondary tourism sources)
visit.dress_code: Dress modestly when visiting religious sites

wat-boromthat.address_line: Klan Kaeo Road, Old Market Area (near Khiri Khet Alley)

history.claim: The temple's ordination hall was built in 1970 (2513 BE) by Mrs. Huatbi.
The ONEP database classifies this temple as a temple, abandoned temple, and religious site, and states that its ordination hall is the smallest in Thailand.
history.quote: the smallest ordination hall in Thailand

history.claim: Evidence confirming the year the temple was founded, its overall founder, its role during the tin mining era, Sino-Portuguese or Chinese characteristics, or its registration as a historical site has not been verified.

timeline.title: Construction of the Small Ordination Hall
timeline.detail: The ordination hall was built by Mrs. Huatbi, featuring a carved stone Buddha image, an inscription, and boundary stones (sema) shaped like Buddha images.

timeline.title: Temple Recorded as Abandoned
timeline.detail: The ONEP database and the National Office of Buddhism's registry list Wat Khuan Tham as an abandoned temple, though the year it was abandoned is not verified.

timeline.title: No Evidence of Historical Site Registration Found
timeline.detail: This search did not find a Fine Arts Department registration announcement specifically confirming Wat Khuha Phimuk in Takua Pa.

history.claim: Municipality documents state that the ordination hall represents Southern local art and uses a wooden pillar as its core.
The municipality notes that the Fine Arts Department registered the ordination hall as a historical site in 1935 (2478 BE); this research has not verified the original registration announcement.

The municipality records a tale that Than Thao, daughter of Phraya Takua Pa (Muang), built the temple in 1777 (2320 BE), but the ONEP database links the establishment of Wat Na Mueang to the founding of the new town during King Rama III's reign; therefore, the construction year is not settled.

The ONEP database explains that the town's revival at Ban Talat Yai during King Rama III's reign began with building Wat Na Mueang before constructing the governor's residence nearby, which differs from the 1777 (2320 BE) tale recorded by the municipality; it is not verified if this was the initial construction or a rebuild.
history.quote: the building of the new town began with building the temple

history.claim: The steam boiler in the temple is a part of a steamboat that Phraya Senanuchit (Nuch Na Nakhon) co-invested with Phraya Wichit Songkhram (That Rattanadilok Na Phuket) to purchase in 1867 (2410 BE) to transport goods and suppress pirates. The boat later deteriorated and sank in the Takua Pa river.

Tourism websites state that the area around the temple once had a large river for transporting goods and minerals, linking this to the discovery of the steam boiler; there is no specific evidence verifying the temple's role in tin mining operations.

The Ban Si Takua Pa Municipal School (Pracharat Rangsan) initially used the monk cells of Wat Pathum Thara as classrooms before moving to Wat Si Nikhom and then to its current location in 1956 (2499 BE); this year refers to the school's relocation, not the temple's construction year.
history.quote: monk cells of Wat Pathum Thara

timeline.title: Tale of the Temple's Construction
timeline.detail: The municipality records a tale that Than Thao, daughter of Phraya Takua Pa (Muang), built Wat Na Mueang this year, but another set of evidence links the temple to the town's revival during King Rama III's reign.

timeline.title: Steamboat and the Takua Pa River
timeline.detail: The steam boiler in the temple area is linked to a steamboat used to transport goods and suppress pirates, co-purchased by Phraya Senanuchit and Phraya Wichit Songkhram.

timeline.title: Ordination Hall Registered as a Historical Site
timeline.detail: The municipality notes that the Fine Arts Department registered the ordination hall, but the original announcement is not verified.

timeline.title: Monk Cells as Initial Classrooms
timeline.detail: The Ban Si Takua Pa Municipal School once held classes in the temple's monk cells before moving to its current location.

timeline.title: Town Revival at Ban Talat Yai
timeline.detail: The ONEP database states that the construction of the new town began with building Wat Na Mueang before constructing the governor's residence nearby.

visit.opening_hours: Love Thailand website specifies every day 08:00 to 17:00, but there is no verified announcement from the temple.

wat-pathum.address_line: Na Mueang Road, Talat Yai Community
